topicName: State Manipulation (import, rm, mv, pull, push)
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Advanced Terraform State Manipulation: import, rm, mv, pull, and push"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Terraform state is the single source of truth for your infrastructure. Knowing how to manipulate the state file directly using CLI commands is essential for maintaining infrastructure without causing downtime or recreation. This tutorial covers the five critical state management commands."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Terraform Import"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The terraform import command is used to bring existing, manually-created resources under Terraform management. First, you must write a configuration block for the resource in your .tf files."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"resource \"aws_instance\" \"web\" {\n  # Configuration goes here\n}"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, run the import command passing the resource address and the provider-specific resource ID."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"terraform import aws_instance.web i-1234567890abcdef0"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Terraform Remove (rm)"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The terraform state rm command removes items from the Terraform state file. This does not destroy the actual cloud resource; it simply stops Terraform from managing it."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"terraform state rm aws_instance.web"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Terraform Move (mv)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"If you refactor your code by renaming resources, changing module structures, or moving resources between state files, terraform state mv is your go-to command to prevent resource recreation."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"terraform state mv aws_instance.old_name aws_instance.new_name"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Terraform Pull"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"The terraform state pull command fetches the current state from the remote backend and outputs it in raw JSON format to stdout. This is useful for inspection or backups."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"terraform state pull > backup_terraform.tfstate"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Terraform Push"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"The terraform state push command uploads a local state file to your remote backend. Note that this command is rarely used in modern workflows as it can easily overwrite remote state and cause race conditions."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"terraform state push custom_terraform.tfstate"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always backup your state file before performing manual state manipulation."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use terraform plan after state operations to verify that no unintended infrastructure changes will occur."}]
